name: Red and blue tail with the eagle
description: White fuselage with 'AirSERBIA' large in navy across the forward windows. The fin split level across about two fifths of the way up: red above, navy below, the flag's colours, with Air Serbia's white eagle mark (a double-headed eagle drawn as interlaced white bands, small blue diamonds between them) straddling the split. Engines red above, a navy band sweeping up toward the exhaust below it, white underneath. Navy wingtips with a small white eagle. A small Serbian flag behind the cockpit and before the registration.

areas.name: navy band under the red, sweeping up toward the exhaust

titles.style: Air Serbia's wordmark in navy across the forward windows from behind the forward door: wide geometric letters with a slight forward lean, 'Air' in upper and lower case, 'SERBIA' in capitals, the A's without crossbars.

logos.description: Air Serbia's eagle: a white double-headed eagle, the two heads facing outward at the top on long necks, its wings and body drawn as white bands looping and interlacing like a woven knot, with small blue diamonds in the gaps between them and a forked tail at the bottom; on the fin's red-navy split, a little below the middle.
The eagle small in white on the navy sharklet.
Small Serbian flag (red, blue, white with the coat of arms) under the cockpit windows' back corner.

notes: Measured on YU-APO (A320, left side from below, Belgrade, 2024-06-10) fitted to the A320 shape; YU-APO (2025), YU-APN (A319, 2024) and YU-APM (A319, 2023, the maintainer's sighting) wear the same. The fin's split runs level across at y 0.38-0.39; the eagle's middle is at (0.5, 0.33), 0.43 of the fin tall. The title runs x 0.169-0.409, its baseline at the windows' bottoms (it reads -0.02 forward to 0.08 aft in the fit, the camera 14° below: drawn level at 0.03), capitals to about y 0.43. The engine's bands are read by eye off the near engine. The belly carries AirSERBIA again in navy (YU-APM from below), not drawn. The A319s have wingtip fences, not sharklets (navy as drawn, not checked). Air Serbia's A330s and ATR 72s are assumed to wear the same scheme; not checked here. Not to be confused with ASL Airlines Belgium (TAY) and the ASL Airlines group.
history: New 2026-11-22 (the maintainer's sightings: YU-APM). Introduced in 2013 when Jat Airways became Air Serbia.
